column1: # Capstone authority / provenance suite — expected runtime outcomes.
#   tag-fault      -> QEMU emits "Cap mem access requires capability" (deref of
#                     an untagged value). The domain must NOT report a retval.
#   bounds-fault   -> QEMU emits "Cap mem access OOB" (deref outside the
#                     capability's bounds). The domain must NOT report a retval.
#   ok             -> domain completes with the exact retval in `detail`
#                     (printed by the host as "retval = <decimal>"), and NO
#   no-trap-today  -> domain completes with the exact numeric retval in `detail`
#                     and WITHOUT any "Cap mem access" fault. This records a
#                     known bounds-granularity gap rather than an intended

column3: inttoptr of a plain integer is untagged
pointer laundered through a volatile integer loses its tag
all-ones unsigned byte index wraps to one byte before the narrowed global
signed byte index -1 lands one byte before the narrowed global

a[100] past a[64]; object SHRINK now narrows a to [a,a+64) so the cross-object over-read traps (was no-trap-today before -capstone-shrink-globals). Run with -mllvm -capstone-shrink-globals=false to see the pre-SHRINK no-trap behaviour.
a[100] past the loadable segment; already trapped today (segment-granular bound)
p[100] past a 64-byte allocation that malloc narrowed with cap_shrink; in-arena but out-of-object, so it traps (heap analogue of global_oob)
